question.text: It is observed that  <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math>  and He gases always show positive deviation from ideal behaviour i.e., Z > 1. This is because

options.text: the value of 'a' is very large due to high attractive forces

the weak intermolecular forces of attraction due to which 'a' is very small and  <math><mfrac><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac></math>  is negligible
the value of 'b' is very large due to large size of the molecules
both 'a' and 'b' are very small and negligible

solution.text: Due to weak intermolecular forces of attraction,  <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math>  and He gases show the value of Z > 1 and always show positive deviation at any pressure.
